Figure.title: Fig. 1 · Distance to the closest record
Figure.caption: Each dot is a synthetic record. Each ring is a real person's record. A dot that lands on a ring can give that person away. Finding those cases is what my thesis is about.
Figure.hint: Move the pointer to audit a record.

About.title: From IoT tinkering to trustworthy AI
About.p1: I started with a B.Tech in Computer Science at Lovely Professional University, with a specialisation in IoT. In 2023 I became a co-inventor on a patent for an internet controlled pet food dispenser.
About.p2: At Coschool I built an AI tutor that reached 1,000+ beta users. That work taught me a model is only as good as how you test it.
About.p3: I moved to Berlin for an MSc in Computer Science with a focus on Big Data and AI. Here I built Klindok, offline software that drafts clinical letters and checks every fact in them. Now I am writing my thesis on privacy audits of synthetic health data.
About.p4: Alongside that I work on the AI side of Kiko, a companion robot, because I want to understand what changes when a model leaves the screen.

ResearchHome.title: What I research, and why
ResearchHome.question: Can an LLM agent find the privacy risks in synthetic health data that standard tests rate as safe?
ResearchHome.coreP1: Hospitals and researchers share synthetic data in place of real patient records. Whether that is safe depends on the test used to check it, and popular tests can miss records that still point to a real person.
ResearchHome.coreP2: The same question runs through everything else I do: measure a system before you trust it.
ResearchHome.thesisBody: Agentic Privacy Auditing of Synthetic Health Data: Evaluating LLM Audit Agents against Attack-Based Re-identification Metrics
ResearchHome.agentsBody: Compared four 2026 surveys where reported adoption ranged from 17% to 65%, and traced why.
ResearchHome.patternsBody: ReAct, Reflection, Planning, Tool use and Multi-agent, matched to real deployments and to MCP and A2A.

ResearchPage.title: Research
ResearchPage.thesisP1: Synthetic health data is meant to keep the patterns of real patient records without containing any real patient. Before it is shared, someone has to check that no synthetic record still points to a real person.
ResearchPage.thesisP2: A common quick check measures how far each synthetic record is from the closest real one, which is what the figure shows. Stronger checks run real attacks against the data and count how often a person can be re-identified.
ResearchPage.thesisP3: My thesis asks whether an LLM agent that audits the same data can find risks that those attack-based metrics rate as low. The work is in progress and there are no results to report yet.
